sanskrit_verse:
ब्रह्महा क्षयरोगी स्यात् सुरापः श्यावदन्तकः ।
हेमहारी तु कुनखी दुश्चर्मा गुरुतल्पगः ॥२०९॥
transliteration: brahmahā kṣayarogī syāt surāpaḥ śyāvadantakaḥ | hemahārī tu kunakhī duścarmā gurutalpagaḥ || 209 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The killer of a Brāhmaṇa shall become consumptive; the drinker of alcohol shall have black teeth; the thief of gold shall lose nails; the violator of guru's bed shall acquire diseased skin.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: Violation of sacred hierarchy incurs ontological consequence.
Causation: Actions align with sequential manifestation of natural dharma.
Capacity-based responsibility: The doer is inherently capable of bearing the consequence.
Restoration logic: Consequence mirrors action to realign consciousness.
Consciousness alignment: Suffering is not punitive but reflective of inner disorder.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, the threshold of responsibility lies in the agent’s capacity to know and act. These consequences are not imposed by court judgment but by the inherent structure of dharma. The Court serves to recognize and declare alignment with this natural sequence rather than enforce it.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality ensures that consequences arise naturally from the act. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as physical and existential reflection of internal disorder. Responsibility is proportional to awareness. There is no external punishment—only the revelation of inner misalignment through form and condition.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Agent must acknowledge the causal link between action and reflection.
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Agent accepts the consequence as self-manifested dharma.
Capacity Restoration: Spiritual practices prescribed to purify the causal body and restore integrity.
Integrity Reintegration: Community facilitates ritual and spiritual correction to realign consciousness.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as sourced dharma. Justice is restoration. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator. Dharma is restored.
